# TimescaleDB upgrade matrix

<!-- Generated by `make matrix`. Edit data/upgrade-matrix.json, not this file. -->

Generated from `data/upgrade-matrix.json` at 2026-10-30T03:50:24Z.

**131 transitions listed — 131 verified, 0 unverified.**

> An `unknown` verdict means nobody has established the answer and written down where it came from. It does **not** mean the upgrade is safe, and it does not mean it is unsafe. Treat these rows as open questions: the tooling refuses to act on them rather than guessing.

A verdict is established only by running that migration with the upgrader itself (`verify/harness.py`), once on an empty database and once on a seeded one. Those runs are not the test suite: each leaves a record of what happened, and the verdict is written from the records. **Evidence** links both records and **PG** is the exact PostgreSQL minor they ran on: a row keyed by a PostgreSQL major is proven only at that minor. A row that changes PostgreSQL major ran both ways again with `pg_upgrade --link` (`link-` records), since `apply` offers it. A `direct-history-` record is a control: the same update without the stop `tsupgrade plan` inserts, run to show the stop is needed. It reads `errored as documented` when it broke the way the row's reason says, and never counts toward the verdict. `no image` rows are verified against the container registry: no such tag is published. **References** are upstream issues, pull requests and release notes that explain a verdict or a caveat; they are never its proof.

A verdict covers TimescaleDB and the route its records ran: the test databases hold `plpgsql` and `timescaledb` and nothing else. Other extensions (PostGIS, `timescaledb_toolkit`, `pg_stat_statements`, ...) are checked by preflight against the measured contents of each image, not by these verdicts.

## Required steps

### pg11/ts2.1 -> pg12/ts2.11

1. pg_upgrade PostgreSQL 11 -> 12 at 2.1.1 with pg12.6-ts2.1.1-p2 (copy, or --link), then start PostgreSQL 12 on pg12.22-ts2.11.2 and re-clone the replicas
1. roll out pg12.22-ts2.11.2 and update to 2.11.2
1. vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages

### pg11/ts2.1 -> pg13/ts2.15

1. pg_upgrade PostgreSQL 11 -> 12 at 2.1.1 with pg12.6-ts2.1.1-p2 (copy, or --link), then start PostgreSQL 12 on pg12.22-ts2.11.2 and re-clone the replicas
1. roll out pg12.22-ts2.11.2 and update to 2.11.2
1. pg_upgrade PostgreSQL 12 -> 13 at 2.11.2 with pg13.12-ts2.11.2-all (copy, or --link), then start PostgreSQL 13 on pg13.22-ts2.15.3 and re-clone the replicas
1. roll out pg13.22-ts2.15.3 and update to 2.15.3
1. after the upgrade, run `CALL cagg_migrate('<aggregate>', override => true, drop_old => true)` on every continuous aggregate created before 2.7, dropping any view on it first and restoring its grants after (measured on 2.14.2 and 2.15.3); it must happen below 2.25, and without those options the old aggregate stays
1. vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages

### pg11/ts2.1 -> pg14/ts2.19

1. pg_upgrade PostgreSQL 11 -> 12 at 2.1.1 with pg12.6-ts2.1.1-p2 (copy, or --link), then start PostgreSQL 12 on pg12.22-ts2.11.2 and re-clone the replicas

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `in place` | The existing data directory can be upgraded without exporting the data. A caveat in the reason still applies. |
| `dump + restore` | The data must be exported and reloaded into a new instance. |
| `unsupported` | This transition is not a supported path. |
| `no image` | No published `timescaledb-ha` image exists for the target pair. |
| `unknown` | Not established. The tooling will not act on it. |
